item.title: Experimental Statistical and Explainable Machine Learning Prediction of Surface Roughness in Cryogenically Pre-Cooled Machining of Inconel 718
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 C S Sumesh
Cryogenic machining offers a sustainable route for improving the machinability of nickel-based superalloys by reducing thermal loading and improving surface quality. This study develops an experimental-statistical-explainable machine learning framework for predicting surface roughness during cryogenically pre-cooled machining of Inconel 718. Spindle speed, feed rate, and depth of cut were varied through a 20-run face-centered central composite design. Each trial was repeated three times, and surface roughness was measured at three locations. The response surface model explained 91.95% of the measured variation and was used to generate a 1,387-point model-based dataset. We report a novel, dynamic, ferroelectric response in ultrathin tetragonal-phase-rich antiferroelectric (AFE) Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 (HZO) films at cryogenic temperatures. At room temperature, AFE switching in these films arises from a field-induced tetragonal-to-orthorhombic (t-to-o) transformation followed by rapid o-to-t back-switching during each switching cycle, retaining little-to-no polar o-phase after applied electric field removal.
